title: SIRD OCR Integration Adversary Model
scope: Task submission and status/result response, RabbitMQ 4.3 task/result/retry/terminal queue transport, Process Service, stateless OCR runtime, PostgreSQL workflow state, RustFS artifacts, and workload identity boundaries shown in security/threat-model/dfd.json and architecture/rendered/sird-ocr-dfd.html.
securityObjectives: Accept task and result operations only from authorized workloads.
Preserve task, attempt, delivery acknowledgement, outbox, artifact, and result integrity.
Prevent unauthorized disclosure of document-derived data, task metadata, and credentials.
Bound resource consumption and preserve queue progress under malformed or failing work.
Keep terminal outcomes and security-relevant actions attributable to a workload identity.

assets.name: Attempt, fencing, retry, outbox, and delivery acknowledgement state
mTLS client certificates, CA trust anchors, and role mappings

attackers.name: Unauthorized external caller
capabilities: Send network requests to an exposed Task Service endpoint
Replay or modify task identifiers and capabilities
cannotAssume: RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, or RustFS network access

attackers.name: Compromised integration workload
attackers.position: inside the application trust zone with one valid workload identity
capabilities: Invoke peer service operations permitted by deployment policy
Submit stale, duplicated, or forged workflow messages
cannotAssume: Valid fencing token for another task
goals: Tamper with workflow state or result events

attackers.name: Malicious or compromised operator
capabilities: Change certificates, ACLs, policies, retention, or deployment configuration
Read service logs and operational stores
cannotAssume: Human approval for production risk acceptance
A valid audit record for unauthorized changes

attackers.name: Malicious document or task producer
attackers.position: authorized SIRD request path but controls the document bytes and task parameters
capabilities: Provide malformed, oversized, compressed, or parser-hostile content
Choose repeated task identifiers within caller authority
goals: Cause incorrect or misleading OCR results

attackers.name: Stolen or mis-issued workload identity
attackers.position: identity boundary with an mTLS client certificate
capabilities: Attempt certificate subject, role, CA trust-anchor, or principal-mapping confusion

assumptionsAndExclusions: The local profile is loopback-only and does not prove production network isolation.
SIRD owns end-user authorization; this integration authorizes workload and task boundaries only.

Host kernel compromise, PostgreSQL superuser compromise, RabbitMQ broker administrator compromise, and CA root compromise are outside this bounded application threat model and require deployment-level review.

Production mTLS client certificate issuance and rotation, CA trust-anchor distribution, RabbitMQ broker authorization, and per-service identity mapping remain production evidence gaps. The local profile validates client certificate material only.
